<!-- Generated by hack/docsgen from internal/config/schema.go; do not edit. Run `make docs-gen`. -->

Every settings key of `kudurru.yaml`, generated from the metadata table in
`internal/config/schema.go`, the same table `kudurru config schema` prints and
`GET /api/v1/settings/_schema` serves.

**Where a value comes from.** Each layer overrides the one before it:

1. the built-in default (the Default column);
2. the config file (`--config`, `KUDURRU_CONFIG`, default `/etc/kudurru/kudurru.yaml`);
3. the settings file (`settingsFile` or `KUDURRU_SETTINGS_FILE`) for cluster-scope keys,
   which is where changes made in the UI, with `kudurru settings set` or with
   `PATCH /api/v1/settings` are written; it is watched and hot keys apply at once;
4. the environment: `KUDURRU_<SECTION>__<KEY>`, with `__` for every dot of the path
   (`KUDURRU_LOG__LEVEL=debug`), or `KUDURRU_<SECTION>__<KEY>_FILE` naming a file
   that holds the value. `string[]` values are comma-separated; `list` and `map` keys
   can only be set in a file. A key set from the environment is read-only in
   the UI, and a variable that names no key stops the server at start.

In Kubernetes, cluster sections default to GitOps ownership. Explicit adoption
of the complete upstreams section enables UI/API writes to a separate shared
ConfigMap; other file keys are never merged into that owned section. Generate
Helm values, apply matching configuration and release ownership to return to
GitOps. See [settings ownership](../../../docs/architecture/configuration-and-store.md#settings).
Docker retains its writable settings-file behavior; explicit ownership is
stored in its settingsOwnership metadata.

**Scope.** `node` keys belong to one host. `cluster` keys are shared by every
node of a deployment.

**Allowed values.** The bold label is the name the UI shows. The *Allowed*
line lists what a key accepts: a closed set, a range, a format (`ip`,
`cidr` for a CIDR or a single address, `hostport`, `url`, `domain`,
`upstream` for a server in dnsproxy syntax), the object a value names (`ref`)
and the members of list and map values. The config file, the environment and
the API reject anything else with an error naming the key.

**Flags.** *host-only* keys can only be set in the file or the environment
on the host, never through the API or the UI (they name listeners, files and
privileged behavior). *restart* keys take effect after a restart (in
Kubernetes the chart rolls the pods); every other key is applied while the
server runs. *write-only* keys are never returned by the API.

## branding

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="branding.name"></a>`branding.name` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Organization name.** Public display name on the dashboard, sign-in and block page. Enterprise only. At most 80 characters; empty uses kudurru. Saved branding is retained when the license no longer permits it.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BRANDING__NAME` |
| <a id="branding.logoLight"></a>`branding.logoLight` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Light logo.** Static PNG data URL for light surfaces, at most 64 KiB decoded and 1024 pixels per dimension. Enterprise only. Empty uses the dark logo if supplied, otherwise built-in artwork. Upload through the Branding editor; remote URLs and SVG are not accepted.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BRANDING__LOGOLIGHT` |
| <a id="branding.logoDark"></a>`branding.logoDark` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Dark logo.** Static PNG data URL for dark surfaces, at most 64 KiB decoded and 1024 pixels per dimension. Enterprise only. Empty uses the light logo if supplied, otherwise built-in artwork. Upload through the Branding editor; remote URLs and SVG are not accepted.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BRANDING__LOGODARK` |
| <a id="branding.favicon"></a>`branding.favicon` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Favicon.** Static PNG data URL for the browser icon, at most 64 KiB decoded and 256 pixels per dimension. Enterprise only. Empty uses the built-in icon. Upload through the Branding editor.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BRANDING__FAVICON` |
| <a id="branding.accentColor"></a>`branding.accentColor` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Accent color.** Six-digit hexadecimal accent color, e.g. #2457A6, for the dashboard and block page. Enterprise only. Accessible text and interaction colors are derived from it; empty keeps the selected theme's accent.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BRANDING__ACCENTCOLOR` |

## response

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="response.dns64.prefix"></a>`response.dns64.prefix` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **DNS64 prefix.** Synthesize IPv6 answers from IPv4 for a NAT64 network. Empty disables DNS64. Use your router's IPv6 /32, /40, /48, /56, /64 or /96 translation prefix, e.g. 64:ff9b::/96. Only AAAA NODATA answers are synthesized; queries requesting DNSSEC proofs keep the original response. A Policy can override this for selected clients.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__DNS64__PREFIX` |
| <a id="response.dns64.excludeDomains"></a>`response.dns64.excludeDomains` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **DNS64 excluded domains.** Domains and descendants excluded from DNS64, e.g. internal.example. At most 256. Both the question and the final alias target are checked.<br>Allowed: items: string (format domain).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__DNS64__EXCLUDEDOMAINS` |
| <a id="response.dns64.excludeIPv4"></a>`response.dns64.excludeIPv4` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **DNS64 excluded IPv4 networks.** IPv4 networks excluded from DNS64, e.g. 192.168.0.0/16. At most 256 canonical CIDRs. Excluded addresses never become synthetic IPv6 answers.<br>Allowed: items: string (format cidr).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__DNS64__EXCLUDEIPV4` |
| <a id="response.filterAAAA"></a>`response.filterAAAA` | `bool` | `false` | cluster | **Filter IPv6 answers.** Remove IPv6 addresses and IPv6 service hints from forwarded responses. AAAA answers become NODATA. This takes precedence over DNS64 and clears DNSSEC authenticity on changed answers. A Policy can override this for selected clients; owned authoritative zones are unaffected.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__FILTERAAAA` |
| <a id="response.bogusNXDOMAIN"></a>`response.bogusNXDOMAIN` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **Redirect addresses treated as NXDOMAIN.** Return NXDOMAIN when a forwarded answer contains an address in one of these networks, for upstreams that redirect missing domains to a search page. At most 256 canonical IPv4 or IPv6 CIDRs. This result is never immediately changed by the NXDOMAIN replacement settings.<br>Allowed: items: string (format cidr).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__BOGUSNXDOMAIN` |
| <a id="response.nxdomainIPv4"></a>`response.nxdomainIPv4` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **NXDOMAIN replacement IPv4 addresses.** Replace upstream NXDOMAIN for A questions with these IPv4 addresses. Empty preserves NXDOMAIN. At most 16 addresses. This deliberately changes validated negative answers and clears AD; rebinding protection still applies to the replacement.<br>Allowed: items: string (format ipv4).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__NXDOMAINIPV4` |
| <a id="response.nxdomainIPv6"></a>`response.nxdomainIPv6` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **NXDOMAIN replacement IPv6 addresses.** Replace upstream NXDOMAIN for AAAA questions with these IPv6 addresses. Empty preserves NXDOMAIN. At most 16 addresses. Disabled for clients with IPv6 filtering enabled; rebinding protection still applies.<br>Allowed: items: string (format ipv6).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__NXDOMAINIPV6` |
| <a id="response.ttl"></a>`response.ttl` | `int` | `300` | cluster | **Synthetic answer TTL (seconds).** Lifetime in seconds for configured rewrites and NXDOMAIN replacements, from 1 to 86400. Also caps DNS64 answers, which cannot outlive their IPv4 answer or the original negative SOA TTL.<br>Allowed: range 1-86400.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__TTL` |
| <a id="response.rebinding.enabled"></a>`response.rebinding.enabled` | `bool` | `false` | cluster | **Protect against DNS rebinding.** Refuse forwarded or rewritten answers containing private, loopback, link-local, unspecified or multicast addresses, including service hints. Configure private-domain exceptions for internal forwarding. Owned authoritative answers and explicit block responses are exempt. An inspection budget overflow also refuses the response.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__REBINDING__ENABLED` |
| <a id="response.rebinding.privateDomains"></a>`response.rebinding.privateDomains` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **Domains allowed private addresses.** Domains allowed to return private addresses, including descendants. At most 256. Both the original question and the address record's owner must be in an allowed domain, so an alias cannot silently escape the exception.<br>Allowed: items: string (format domain).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__REBINDING__PRIVATEDOMAINS` |
| <a id="response.rebinding.bypassNetworks"></a>`response.rebinding.bypassNetworks` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **Clients exempt from rebinding protection.** Client networks exempt from rebinding protection. At most 256 canonical IPv4 or IPv6 CIDRs. Empty protects all clients; an explicit /0 disables protection for that address family.<br>Allowed: items: string (format cidr).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RESPONSE__REBINDING__BYPASSNETWORKS` |

## control

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="control.allowedNetworks"></a>`control.allowedNetworks` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **Allowed client networks.** Client networks allowed to query DNS, for example 192.168.1.0/24 or fd00::/64. Empty allows all clients; loopback always passes this network check. Other clients receive REFUSED before local, cached or upstream answers. At most 1024 IPv4 or IPv6 CIDRs; changes take effect without restart.<br>Allowed: items: string (format cidr).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CONTROL__ALLOWEDNETWORKS` |
| <a id="control.blockedQTypes"></a>`control.blockedQTypes` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **Blocked query types.** DNS query types refused for every client, including loopback, for example ANY or HINFO. Empty blocks none. At most 256 case-insensitive DNS mnemonics or explicit TYPE1 through TYPE65535 values; changes take effect before local, cached or upstream answers without restart. Malformed queries still drop silently.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CONTROL__BLOCKEDQTYPES` |

## dnssec

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="dnssec.enabled"></a>`dnssec.enabled` | `bool` | `false` | cluster | **Validate DNSSEC.** Validate forwarded DNS answers against the configured trust anchors. Invalid or incomplete proofs return SERVFAIL with an extended DNS error; unsigned delegations still work. Off by default for compatibility. A forward zone can override this default with spec.forward.dnssecValidation.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DNSSEC__ENABLED` |
| <a id="dnssec.useBuiltinAnchors"></a>`dnssec.useBuiltinAnchors` | `bool` | `true` | cluster | **Use built-in root trust anchors.** Trust the IANA root DS records shipped with this version. Software upgrades or an operator change maintain these anchors; no keys are trusted automatically from upstream responses. Turn off only when dnssec.trustAnchors supplies all trust roots you need.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DNSSEC__USEBUILTINANCHORS` |
| <a id="dnssec.trustAnchors"></a>`dnssec.trustAnchors` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **Additional trust anchors.** Additional trusted DS or DNSKEY records in DNS presentation format, e.g. a complete DS record for a private signed zone. At most 64. With useBuiltinAnchors off these replace the shipped root anchors, and at least one is required. Changes invalidate the old validation cache context immediately.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DNSSEC__TRUSTANCHORS` |
| <a id="dnssec.negativeTrustAnchors"></a>`dnssec.negativeTrustAnchors` | `list` | `[]` | cluster | **Temporary validation exceptions.** Temporary exceptions for broken signed domains (RFC 7646); at most 128. Every exception needs a reason and an absolute expiry no more than seven days away. It covers the domain and descendants, never sets AD, and stops applying at expiry even on cache hits. Reload and restart do not extend it.<br>Allowed: items: {domain (required): string (format domain); reason (required): string; expiresAt (required): string (format date-time)}.<br>Environment: file only. |

## node

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="node.name"></a>`node.name` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Node name.** Name of this server in the dashboard, the query log and the block page, e.g. dns1. Empty uses the hostname. Every node of a cluster needs its own name; it identifies the node to the others.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_NODE__NAME` |
| <a id="node.lameduck"></a>`node.lameduck` | `duration` | `2s` | node | **Lameduck drain window.** How long the server keeps answering after it is told to stop, so devices and load balancers move to another server first, e.g. 2s; 0 stops at once. During this window readiness (/healthz/ready) answers 503 and the health name SERVFAIL, then the listeners close. The Helm chart also runs kudurru lameduck in preStop.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_NODE__LAMEDUCK` |
| <a id="node.dataDir"></a>`node.dataDir` | `string` | `/var/lib/kudurru` | node | **Data directory.** Directory where kudurru keeps its data, e.g. /var/lib/kudurru; it must be writable and should survive restarts and be backed up. It holds the object store (state.db), downloaded lists and keys. The query log (querylog.db) and local state (local.db) also live here unless node.querylogDir or node.localDir selects a separate directory.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_NODE__DATADIR` |
| <a id="node.querylogDir"></a>`node.querylogDir` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Query log directory.** Directory for querylog.db and its SQLite sidecars. Empty keeps node.dataDir. Use a clean absolute path on writable node-local storage; stop the server and copy existing files before changing it. No files move automatically. Restart required.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_NODE__QUERYLOGDIR` |
| <a id="node.localDir"></a>`node.localDir` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Local state directory.** Directory for local.db and its SQLite sidecars: snapshots, transferred zones and the response cache. Empty keeps node.dataDir. Use a clean absolute path on writable node-local storage; migrate files while stopped and restart. Independent volumes do not form an atomic backup.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_NODE__LOCALDIR` |

## dhcp

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="dhcp.enabled"></a>`dhcp.enabled` | `bool` | `false` | node | **DHCPv4 enabled.** Assign IPv4 addresses on configured direct or trusted-relay LAN scopes. Disabled by default; requires Linux and, with store.driver sqlite, a complete DHCP configuration; with store.driver kube, scopes are DHCPScope objects and one replica serves through a relay to the dhcp.serverIP LoadBalancer address. Restart to apply changes. Supports named scopes, trusted relays and optional local DNS records; Optional three-node quorum failover replicates ownership; DHCPv6 is not supported.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__ENABLED` |
| <a id="dhcp.interface"></a>`dhcp.interface` | `string` | (empty) | node | **LAN interface.** Network interface serving the LAN, e.g. eth0. Required when DHCP is enabled; the server binds UDP port 67 on this interface and verifies that dhcp.serverIP is assigned to it. With store.driver kube: the pod interface receiving relayed packets, default eth0.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__INTERFACE` |
| <a id="dhcp.serverIP"></a>`dhcp.serverIP` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Server IPv4 address.** Static IPv4 address of this server on the LAN, e.g. 192.168.1.2. Required when enabled, must be on the host interface and, for a direct scope, a usable address in dhcp.subnet; it is never assigned to clients. With store.driver kube: the LoadBalancer address relays send to, advertised as the server identifier.<br>Allowed: format ipv4.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__SERVERIP` |
| <a id="dhcp.subnet"></a>`dhcp.subnet` | `string` | (empty) | node | **LAN subnet.** IPv4 network of the LAN in CIDR notation, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24. Required when enabled; use the network address, with enough host addresses for the server and clients.<br>Allowed: format cidr.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__SUBNET` |
| <a id="dhcp.rangeStart"></a>`dhcp.rangeStart` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Dynamic range start.** First IPv4 address of the inclusive dynamic range, e.g. 192.168.1.100. Required when enabled and must be in dhcp.subnet, no higher than dhcp.rangeEnd. Server, router and reserved addresses are excluded from allocation. In management=api scopes, live values are owned by the DHCP API and lease database; these host values seed the first start.<br>Allowed: format ipv4.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__RANGESTART` |
| <a id="dhcp.rangeEnd"></a>`dhcp.rangeEnd` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Dynamic range end.** Last IPv4 address of the inclusive dynamic range, e.g. 192.168.1.200. Required when enabled and must be in dhcp.subnet, no lower than dhcp.rangeStart. In management=api scopes, live values are owned by the DHCP API and lease database; these host values seed the first start.<br>Allowed: format ipv4.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__RANGEEND` |
| <a id="dhcp.router"></a>`dhcp.router` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Default gateway.** IPv4 default gateway advertised to clients, e.g. 192.168.1.1. Required when enabled, must be a usable address in the client subnet and is never assigned to clients. In management=api scopes, live values are owned by the DHCP API and lease database; these host values seed the first start.<br>Allowed: format ipv4.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__ROUTER` |
| <a id="dhcp.dnsServers"></a>`dhcp.dnsServers` | `string[]` | `[]` | node | **Client DNS servers.** IPv4 DNS servers advertised to clients in order, e.g. \[192.168.1.2\]. When enabled, specify 1 to 63 unicast IPv4 addresses. Set this explicitly to advertise kudurru; the existing DNS listeners are unchanged. In management=api scopes, live values are owned by the DHCP API and lease database; these host values seed the first start.<br>Allowed: items: string (format ipv4).<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__DNSSERVERS` |
| <a id="dhcp.domainName"></a>`dhcp.domainName` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Client domain name.** Domain name advertised to clients, e.g. home.example; empty omits the domain-name option. With registerDNS enabled, bound leases publish names in this domain outside configured DNS zones. In management=api scopes, live values are owned by the DHCP API and lease database; these host values seed the first start.<br>Allowed: format domain.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__DOMAINNAME` |
| <a id="dhcp.leaseDuration"></a>`dhcp.leaseDuration` | `duration` | `12h` | node | **Lease duration.** How long an acknowledged address assignment lasts, e.g. 12h. When enabled, use whole seconds from 1m through 720h (30 days); clients renew before it expires. In management=api scopes, live values are owned by the DHCP API and lease database; these host values seed the first start.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__LEASEDURATION` |
| <a id="dhcp.reservations"></a>`dhcp.reservations` | `list` | `[]` | node | **Address reservations.** IPv4 addresses reserved for devices by Ethernet MAC, with an optional hostname. Reserved addresses are excluded from the dynamic pool and may be elsewhere in dhcp.subnet. Hostnames also name local records when registerDNS is enabled. In management=api scopes, live values are owned by the DHCP API and lease database; these host values seed the first start.<br>Allowed: items: {mac (required): string; ip (required): string (format ipv4); hostname: string (format domain)}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="dhcp.management"></a>`dhcp.management` | `string` | `file` | node | **Management owner.** Scope ownership: file keeps host settings authoritative; api seeds pool options and reservations from the config file once and persists live edits in dhcp.db. Enabled API-managed scopes reject mutable environment overrides; remove them or use file management. Change ownership on the host, then restart.<br>Allowed: one of file \| api.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__MANAGEMENT` |
| <a id="dhcp.relayOnly"></a>`dhcp.relayOnly` | `bool` | `false` | node | **Relay-only scope.** Serve this scope only through configured trusted relays; serverIP may be outside the client subnet. Host topology requires restart.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__RELAYONLY` |
| <a id="dhcp.trustedRelays"></a>`dhcp.trustedRelays` | `list` | `[]` | node | **Trusted DHCP relays.** Exact relay sourceIP and gatewayIP pairs trusted on the configured interface. Gateway addresses cannot be allocated. Set on the host and restart.<br>Allowed: items: {sourcePort: int (range 0-65535); linkSelection: string (format ipv4); serverIdentifier: string (format ipv4); sourceIP (required): string (format ipv4); gatewayIP (required): string (format ipv4)}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="dhcp.registerDNS"></a>`dhcp.registerDNS` | `bool` | `false` | node | **Register local DNS records.** Publish bound-lease A/PTR records under a dedicated domainName when no zone matches or the match is the catch-all root forward zone. Specific zones and a primary root retain precedence. In management=api scopes this option is changed through the DHCP API; this host value is a seed.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__REGISTERDNS` |
| <a id="dhcp.dnsTTL"></a>`dhcp.dnsTTL` | `duration` | `30s` | node | **Local DNS TTL.** Maximum TTL of generated local DNS records, whole seconds from 1s to 1h, clamped to the remaining lease. In management=api scopes use the DHCP API for live edits.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_DHCP__DNSTTL` |
| <a id="dhcp.scopes"></a>`dhcp.scopes` | `list` | `[]` | node | **DHCPv4 scopes.** Named DHCPv4 scopes. Mutually exclusive with legacy flat scope fields; each scope has host-only topology and file or API ownership. API-managed pool options and reservations are durable and live; use the DHCP API rather than generic settings writes.<br>Allowed: items: {name (required): string; management: string (one of file \| api, default file); interface (required): string; serverIP (required): string (format ipv4); subnet (required): string (format cidr); relayOnly: bool (default false); trustedRelays: list of {sourcePort: int (range 0-65535); linkSelection: string (format ipv4); serverIdentifier: string (format ipv4); sourceIP (required): string (format ipv4); gatewayIP (required): string (format ipv4)}; rangeStart (required): string (format ipv4); rangeEnd (required): string (format ipv4); router (required): string (format ipv4); dnsServers (required): list of string (format ipv4); domainName: string (format domain); leaseDuration: duration (default 12h); reservations: list of {mac (required): string; ip (required): string (format ipv4); hostname: string (format domain)}; registerDNS: bool (default false); dnsTTL: duration (default 30s); conflictDetection: string (one of auto \| arp \| icmp \| disabled); probeTimeout: duration; ntpServers: list of string (format ipv4); domainSearch: list of string (format domain); classlessRoutes: list of {destination (required): string (format cidr); router (required): string (format ipv4)}; bootServer: string (format ipv4); bootServerName: string; bootFile: string; bootProfiles: list of {architecture (required): int (range 0-65535); bootServer: string (format ipv4); bootServerName: string; bootFile: string}; failoverServers: list of {nodeID (required): string; address (required): string (format ipv4)}}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |
